assessment: The incumbent directly previews embedded captions in the required delivery format and retains earlier previews. It reached the intended preview within 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions. Repeated saves, variable render times and completion inversions could jointly create waiting and identification work, but their causal contributions are unmeasured. H1-O4 establishes expectation mismatches, including one previous video cut; it does not locate the fault in selection, input binding or rendering. H1-O7 limits any claim that full rendering inherently prevents timely, unambiguous previews: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes. The 49-hour sampled week does not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each request to retained, immutable video and caption revisions, carry their hashes through rendering, and display that pairing consistently on the completed preview and download.
openings.delta: Replace reliance on separately named captions and completion-numbered previews with an inspectable intended pair; retain a pinned last-delivered pair and its original captions.
openings.prediction: When jobs finish out of order or sources change during rendering, outputs still match their recorded requested pair and editors identify the intended pair more reliably.
openings.probe: In private staging, use fabricated footage to interleave two video cuts and caption revisions, including delayed jobs and edits after submission. Compare requested and output hashes and have both editors select the final intended pair. Verify the previous delivery remains retrievable with its original wording.
assumptions: Revision retention and request metadata can be added within four engineer-days and one editor-day.
The current worker can consume fixed revisions within the existing processing allowance.
Clear pairing labels are understandable to editors.

openings.claim: Does excess time after the final edit primarily precede availability of the correct preview or follow its availability?
openings.delta: Distinguish processing delay from locating and checking an already available result before choosing further changes.
openings.prediction: A processing explanation predicts most excess time occurs before correct-output availability; an identification explanation predicts it occurs afterward. Mixed intervals would support a combined account.
openings.probe: Use existing render timestamps and brief staged replays with both editors to record final save, correct-output availability, first correct selection and confirmation. Include single-correction and repeated-save histories; separate watching time from selection time and record incorrect choices.
assumptions: A small replay sample fits the shared editor-day and remaining engineering allowance.
Staged behavior is informative but requires confirmation in the 30 new sessions.
